hints: Look closely at product Y and count its carbons and functional groups, it has both a ketone and a carboxylic acid.
Remember what hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ does to a C=C bond, a $\text{C-H}$ end becomes $\text{-COOH}$ and a $\text{C-alkyl}$ end becomes a ketone.
Work backwards from Y to rebuild the ring, the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ and the acid $\text{-COOH}$ ends must have been joined as C=C in a five membered ring.
walkthrough:
**Describe product Y**

Look at Y with love. It is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$.

It is a 6-carbon open chain with a ketone on the left and a carboxylic acid on the right. That combination screams ring opening by oxidation.

**Recall oxidative cleavage of alkenes**

With hot concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4$, the C=C bond is completely broken in a single step:
$$\text{RCH=CR}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{conc. KMnO}_4} \text{RCOOH} + \text{R}_2\text{C=O}$$

So $\text{=CH-}$ gives an acid, and $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)-}$ gives a methyl ketone.

**Test option A forwards**

Option A is 1,3-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene. Label the double bond $\text{C1}(\text{CH}_3\text{)=C2(H)-}$.

Break $\text{C1=C2}$. $\text{C1}$ has a methyl so becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O-}$. $\text{C2}$ has a H so becomes $\text{HOOC-}$. The rest of the ring $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}(\text{CH}_3\text{)-}$ stays in the middle. That gives exactly:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}(\text{CH}_3\text{)-COOH}$$
Which is Y.

**Conclude the match**

Only a 5-membered ring with methyls in the 1 and 3 positions gives the correct carbon skeleton, with the branch on the carbon next to the acid. That is exactly option A.

options.A: 1,3-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene cleaved at $\text{(CH}_3\text{)C=CH-}$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ at one end and $\text{-COOH}$ at the other, with the $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-}$ bridge in between. This is exactly Y, 2-methyl-5-oxohexanoic acid.
options.B: This is the 1,4-isomer with the second methyl on the carbon opposite the double bond. Cleavage would give $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, the 3-methyl isomer, not the 2-methyl isomer Y.
options.C: This is a six-membered ring, 1,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene. Ring opening would give a 7-carbon chain ($6+1$ extra methyl on cleavage, one methyl stays as branch), too long for the 6-carbon Y. Students choosing this forget to count total carbons.
options.D: This is 1,2-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene where both C=C carbons carry methyls. Cleavage gives a diketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{-COCH}_3$, with no carboxylic acid and too many carbons. It cannot give a keto-acid like Y.
